The scanner boarded one name — DLB, a Type A bearish post-earnings gap graded A — but it printed on near-zero relative volume (0.01x vs the 1.3x bar), the weakest confirmation possible. Honor the board as watch-only; sell nothing new today and re-run tomorrow.

focus.jnote: The scanner boarded a name, but the tape is still fragile and the one setup is thin — that's the signal. On Tuesday the S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53, its lowest close since late July, and the Dow dropped 1.64% to 50,759. The VIX jumped 11.13% to 25.46, its fourth consecutive higher close, up from Monday's 22.91. After the bell the mood improved: Nvidia rose about 3% after hours as revenue of $115.84 billion topped the ~$109 billion estimate and adjusted EPS of $2.68 beat $2.48, and it guided fourth-quarter revenue to about $130 billion. That lifted pre-open futures — US S&P 500 e-mini futures clung to gains, up 0.3%, with the VIX easing toward ~24.5. But one print doesn't erase a four-day slide, and the day's scheduled risk is macro: the FOMC releases minutes from its October meeting at 2:00 PM Eastern on 18 November, with CME FedWatch showing a ~97% chance of a 25bp December hike. A Sniper does not open new premium into that.
focus.notdown: AI/chip names caught a relief bid overnight as Nvidia's beat reassured the complex — NVDA was up ~2.85% pre-market and futures steadied after it cleared its earnings bar. But none of these boarded as clean Snipers, and chasing a one-day relief bounce in a tape that just made a five-month low is exactly the trap 4-VAL guards against. The only name the scanner boarded is bearish (DLB), not a bullish chip. Watch-only.
focus.notup: DLB (Dolby) is the natural bearish lean — it beat on EPS but guided fiscal-2027 revenue and margins flattish, and the stock fell ~8% Tuesday. The scanner boarded it Type A / Grade A bearish. But the honest problem: it printed on near-zero relative volume (0.01x vs the 1.3x confirmation bar), and selling a bear call into a possible NVDA-driven relief rally with FOMC minutes at 2PM carries two-sided squeeze risk. Sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Three things stack. One: P(≥1% gap) at ~42% is above the 35% trigger and composite 58 is WARM — either locks out GREEN. Two: FOMC October minutes release at 2:00 PM ET today into a tape pricing a ~97% December hike — a scheduled macro event inside 24h that independently bars a GREEN verdict. Three: the one boarded name (DLB) is honored on the board but printed its gap on near-zero relative volume (0.01x) — the weakest possible confirmation for a post-earnings move, and its guidance read is soft but not a slam-dunk miss. Stand down on new credit spreads, treat the board as watch-only, and re-run tomorrow. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: Audio/video licensor that fell ~8% Tuesday and another ~5% after hours on its fiscal-Q4 report — the stock dropped after hours to about $56 after closing the regular session at $58.82, down 3.83%. The print itself was a beat — results surpassed Wall Street expectations, with the average Zacks estimate at $1.19 per share vs the reported $1.25 — so the gap is being driven by guidance, not the quarter: management said fiscal 2027 revenue and operating margins are expected to be flattish, which likely overshadowed the modest beat. The scanner boarded it Type A / Grade A bearish. Honest concerns the row must carry: reaction-day relative volume was ~0.01x — far below the 1.3x confirmation bar — the weakest possible read for a post-earnings move, and three S/R layers sit ABOVE price (swing ~$57.79, gap-floor $58.82, swing ~$59.97), any of which can cap a bear-call short strike nicely but also marks resistance the stock could reclaim. Next earnings ~2/16/27, safely outside DTE. Open interest didn't return — verify manually; ATM spread $0.25 OK (bar $0.28).

DLB gap printed on near-zero volume — the only boarded name is a Type A bearish post-earnings gap, but its reaction-day relative volume was ~0.01x vs the 1.3x bar. A gap on almost no volume is weakly confirmed and prone to reversal; do not confuse Tuesday’s ~8% drop with a volume-validated move, especially into a possible NVDA-relief squeeze.

Strait of Hormuz & oil — a +5.28M-barrel crude inventory build pulled WTI lower despite ongoing U.S.–Iran aerial strikes and Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks. Easing now, but any re-escalation sends crude and the geopolitical premium vertical — a live tail.
